_about: Curated, operator-maintained data for offshore-north-dashboard.html (the companion page to the Offshore North podcast). Everything here is dated and sourced; the live pieces (latest campaign posts, latest headlines) come from api/offshore_north_dashboard.json, refreshed by scripts/fetch_offshore_north_dashboard.py. Update this file after a milestone, a result, or a position fix — never invent a fix. Verified 2026-09-14 against the URLs in each entry.

campaign.skipper_line: President and skipper. Came to the sport from engineering and business (26 years leading JMP Solutions). Holds the double-handed course record for the RORC Transatlantic Race; 4th in the 2024 New York Vendée, his first solo IMOCA race. Collingwood, Ontario.
campaign.goal: Become the first Canadian to finish the Vendée Globe — solo, non-stop, unassisted around the world — at the 2028 edition.
campaign.initiative: Be Water Positive (water-scarcity awareness) + a Youth Pathway Programme for young Canadian sailors.
campaign.entry_name: Canada Ocean Racing – Be Water Positive
campaign.tracker_provider: YB Tracking (the team's own public tracker page)

pedigree.text: Won The Ocean Race as Mālama (11th Hour Racing Team, Charlie Enright)
4th, New York Vendée (Sébastien Simon, as Groupe Dubreuil)
3rd in the Vendée Globe with Sébastien Simon, most of the course on one foil after early-December damage; solo 24-hour record on this hull
Acquired by Canada Ocean Racing, renamed EMIRA IV; 6th in The Ocean Race Europe; retired from the Rolex Fastnet Race

Delivered France → Canada (Atlantic, St Lawrence Seaway, Welland Canal, Great Lakes); first Canadian summer training programme on Georgian Bay, June–August; departed Collingwood 8–9 August; heading back to Europe (team post, 2 September)

position_log.text: Arrived in Collingwood, Ontario, for the summer training programme on Georgian Bay.
Departed Collingwood (weekend of 8–9 August), earlier than the published mid-August plan.
Welland Canal transit posted on the team's YouTube channel.
"Emira IV now leaving Canada and heading back to Europe" — Scott's Notes, Thank you, Canada.

outline: Complete at least one Grade 2 solo race from the IMOCA 2025–2028 calendar on the boat you will race in the Vendée Globe, finishing within twice the winner's time.
Be among the top 37 in the IMOCA Globe Series championship (remaining places under the organisers' criteria).
The fleet is capped at 40 boats.

lineage.text: Won the very first Route du Rhum in 1978 — 47 years old, in the 12-metre trimaran Olympus Photo, by 98 seconds after 23 days at sea. He died in 2022, aged 90.

Lying second in the 1996–97 Vendée Globe when his last message from the South Pacific described 15-metre seas and 80-knot winds. Never heard from again; wreckage of Groupe LG 2 reached Chile months later.
Campaigned Spirit of Canada through the round-the-world races of the 2000s and started a Vendée Globe; no Vendée finish. Died in 2016.
Chapter four. No Canadian has ever completed the Vendée Globe.
